description: Open Power System Data (OPSD) is a free data platform for power system modelling. The project, run by researchers at Neon, TU Berlin, ETH Zürich and DIW, collects, checks, processes and documents data that are publicly available but inconvenient to use, and republishes them as data packages with a citable DOI per version. Five core packages exist: time series of electricity load (actual and forecast from the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform), wind and solar generation, capacities, generation profiles and day-ahead prices for 32 European countries, by country, control area or bidding zone, at 15, 30 and 60 minute resolution from 2015 to September 2020; conventional power plants with unit-level capacity, fuel, technology and location for 17 European countries; renewable power plants for eight countries (Czechia, Denmark, France, Germany, Poland, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom); national generation capacity by technology for 1990 to 2020; and weather data. Contributed packages add household load data, wind and solar profiles and When2Heat heat-demand profiles (updated July 2023). Each package is offered as CSV, Excel and SQLite files with a datapackage.json describing fields and sources, downloadable without registration at no cost. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): MIT for the processing scripts, CC-BY for the website text; data packages keep the licences of their original sources. Caveats: the core packages were last released between August and October 2020 and are not updated. The data serve network flow, capacity planning and optimisation studies of the European power system as load and generation inputs. No other catalogued records relate directly yet.

Core package versions: time series 2020-10-06, conventional plants and national capacity 2020-10-01, renewable plants 2020-08-25, weather 2020-09-16.
